Both follow a strict vocabullary based on Genomic Standards Consortium MIxS Data Standard's BioticRelationshipEnum (https://genomicsstandardsconsortium.github.io/mixs/BioticRelationshipEnum/)

The syntactic scope is the exact same. However the syntactic representation in different. Here, the object MIxS may receive two values the host scientific name and/or comma-separated to its NCBI taxonomic ID (host scientific name, taxonomy ID); while the subject expects only one, the latter (NCBI taxid)
Both expect a value from the Human Disease Ontology for humans (https://www.disease-ontology.org), while non-human hosts are free text.
Both standards expect values from a controlled vocabulary. Both controlled vocabularies are the same.

For both standards, values for this field is specific to the taxa associated with the entry. For virus/paghes: lytic, lysogenic, temperate, obligately lytic are allowed. For plasmid: incompatibility group. For eukaryote: asexual, sexual; other more specific values (e.g., incompatibility group) are also allowed.
Both standards expect a specific range of values (DwC:https://rs.gbif.org/vocabulary/dna/rel_to_oxygen.xml; MIxS: https://genomicsstandardsconsortium.github.io/mixs/RelToOxygenEnum/)

The example seems to be switched with the samp_collec_method. DwC seems to allow for various devices to be enumerated (comma separated), not sure if MIxS also allows for this as there are no examples provided. For both standards, they mention the ability to accept terms listed under specimen collection device from the Genomic Epidemiology Ontology, however the term has been deprecated (https://ontobee.org/ontology/GENEPIO?iri=http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GENEPIO_0002094).
The example provideded in DwC and the structured/Regex pattern mentioned in MIxS don't seem to align.

Both standards expect a quality designation along with a percentage of completeness, according to 'High Quality Draft: >90%, Medium Quality Draft: >50%, and Low Quality Draft: < 50%'. It is expected that an abbreviation is made for the quality designation and that a semi-colon separated the percentage (quality;percent completeness).

DwC does too (https://rs.gbif.org/vocabulary/dna/compl_appr.xml), however for 'other' option, it allows users to specifiy wich other approach was used ('other: UViG length compared to the average length of reference genomes from the P22virus genus (NCBI RefSeq v83)'). In a previous version MIxS also allowed for this (https://genomicsstandardsconsortium.github.io/mixs/0000071/).

Both standards expect values from a controlled vocabulary. Both controlled vocabularies are the same. However multiple values are handled differently. In DwC, plurality is handled by adding 'and' between different parameters. This was also the case for a previous version of MIxS, however, currently, MIxS accepts multiple values separated by paragraphs??

DwC presents a controlled vocabulary (https://rs.gbif.org/vocabulary/dna/bin_software.xml). When multiple software are to be reported, DwC expects 'and' to separate them (example: concoct and maxbin), while MIxS expects ',' with the version between parenthesis (example: MetaCluster-TA (RRID:SCR_004599), MaxBin (biotools:maxbin)).
